chapters.title: Matrices and Determinants

content.overview:
A matrix is a rectangular arrangement of numbers. Matrices are used to organise data and solve systems of linear equations. A
determinant is a scalar associated with a square matrix.
study_notes: For A = [a■■], the order is number of rows × number of columns.
Two matrices can be added only when they have the same order.
For a 2 × 2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]], det(A) = ad − bc.
A square matrix is invertible when its determinant is non-zero; A■¹ = adj(A)/det(A).
For compatible matrices, generally AB ≠ BA.
content.short_questions:
What is a square matrix?

   Answer: A matrix with the same number of rows and columns.
When does a 2 × 2 matrix have an inverse?

   Answer: When its determinant is non-zero.
content.long_questions:
Find the determinant and inverse of A = [[2,1],[5,3]].

   Solution: det(A) = 2×3 − 1×5 = 1. The adjugate is [[3,−1],[−5,2]]. Therefore A■¹ = [[3,−1],[−5,2]].

mcqs.content: The determinant of [[a,b],[c,d]] is: A. ad − bc B. ab − cd C. ac − bd D. ad + bc Answer: A
A square matrix is singular if its determinant is: A. 1 B. −1 C. 0 D. Non-zero Answer: C

1ST PAPER — Chapter 1: Matrices and Determinants
Chapter overview
A matrix is a rectangular arrangement of numbers. Matrices are used to organise data and solve systems of linear equations. A
determinant is a scalar associated with a square matrix.

Key concepts and important formulas
• For A = [a■■], the order is number of rows × number of columns.

• Two matrices can be added only when they have the same order.

• For a 2 × 2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]], det(A) = ad − bc.

• A square matrix is invertible when its determinant is non-zero; A■¹ = adj(A)/det(A).

• For compatible matrices, generally AB ≠ BA.

Short-answer practice — answers
What is a square matrix?

   Answer: A matrix with the same number of rows and columns.
When does a 2 × 2 matrix have an inverse?

   Answer: When its determinant is non-zero.

Long-answer practice — worked solution
Find the determinant and inverse of A = [[2,1],[5,3]].

   Solution: det(A) = 2×3 − 1×5 = 1. The adjugate is [[3,−1],[−5,2]]. Therefore A■¹ = [[3,−1],[−5,2]].

Multiple-choice questions
1. The determinant of [[a,b],[c,d]] is:

A. ad − bc     B. ab − cd   C. ac − bd   D. ad + bc

Answer: A

2. A square matrix is singular if its determinant is:

A. 1   B. −1    C. 0   D. Non-zero

Answer: C

Exam tip: State the formula or theorem, show the substitution and algebraic steps, and include units or domain restrictions where relevant.

chapters.title: Vectors

content.overview:
A vector has magnitude and direction. Vectors describe displacement, velocity and force. Vector operations allow geometric and
physical quantities to be resolved and combined.
study_notes: In two dimensions, a = a■i + a■j.
Magnitude: |a| = √(a■² + a■²).
Dot product: a·b = |a||b|cosθ; it is a scalar.
Cross-product magnitude: |a×b| = |a||b|sinθ.
The resultant of vectors is found by adding corresponding components.
content.short_questions:
Bangladesh HSC Higher Mathematics | First & Second Paper                                                                                      Page 3

What is a unit vector?

   Answer: A vector of magnitude one that specifies direction.
When is the dot product zero?

   Answer: When the two non-zero vectors are perpendicular.
content.long_questions:
Find the magnitude and direction of v = 3i + 4j.

   Solution: |v| = √(3²+4²) = 5. Its angle from the positive x-axis is θ = tan■¹(4/3) ≈ 53.13°.

mcqs.content: The magnitude of 3i + 4j is: A. 3 B. 4 C. 5 D. 7 Answer: C
If a·b = 0 for two non-zero vectors, the angle is: A. 0° B. 45° C. 90° D. 180° Answer: C

content.answer_tip: Exam tip: State the formula or theorem, show the substitution and algebraic steps, and include units or domain restrictions where relevant.

What is a unit vector?

   Answer: A vector of magnitude one that specifies direction.
When is the dot product zero?

   Answer: When the two non-zero vectors are perpendicular.

Long-answer practice — worked solution
Find the magnitude and direction of v = 3i + 4j.

   Solution: |v| = √(3²+4²) = 5. Its angle from the positive x-axis is θ = tan■¹(4/3) ≈ 53.13°.

Multiple-choice questions
1. The magnitude of 3i + 4j is:

A. 3    B. 4   C. 5     D. 7

chapters.title: Straight Lines

content.overview:
Coordinate geometry represents geometric objects using equations. A straight line may be described by its slope and a point, two
points, intercepts or a general linear equation.
study_notes: Slope m = (y■−y■)/(x■−x■), where x■ ≠ x■.
Point-slope form: y−y■ = m(x−x■).
Slope-intercept form: y = mx+c.
Parallel non-vertical lines have equal slopes; perpendicular lines satisfy m■m■ = −1.
The general form is ax+by+c=0.
content.short_questions:
What is the slope of a horizontal line?

   Answer: Zero.
State the condition for two non-vertical lines to be perpendicular.

   Answer: Their slopes have product −1.
content.long_questions:
Find the equation of the line through (2,3) and (4,7).

   Solution: Slope m = (7−3)/(4−2) = 2. Using y−3 = 2(x−2), the equation is y = 2x−1.

mcqs.content: The slope of a line parallel to y = 5x + 2 is: A. −5 B. 1/5 C. 5 D. 2 Answer: C
A vertical line has equation: A. y = constant B. x = constant C. y = mx+c D. x+y=0 Answer: B Bangladesh HSC Higher Mathematics | First & Second Paper Page 4

chapters.title: Circles

content.overview: A circle is the locus of points at a fixed distance from a fixed centre. Its equation follows from the distance formula.
study_notes: Standard form: (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r².
Centre-radius form x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 has centre (−g,−f).
Radius = √(g²+f²−c).
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
A point lies inside, on or outside a circle according as its centre distance is less than, equal to or greater than r.
content.short_questions:
What is the radius of x²+y²=r²?

   Answer: The radius is r and the centre is (0,0).
What is the relation between a tangent and the radius at contact?

   Answer: They are perpendicular.
content.long_questions:
Find the centre and radius of x²+y²−4x+6y−12=0.

   Solution: Complete squares: (x−2)²−4+(y+3)²−9−12=0. Thus (x−2)²+(y+3)²=25. Centre = (2,−3), radius = 5.

mcqs.content: The radius of x²+y²=49 is: A. 5 B. 7 C. 14 D. 49 Answer: B
A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the: A. Diameter anywhere B. Radius at contact C. Chord always D. Secant Answer: B

content.answer_tip: Exam tip: State the formula or theorem, show the substitution and algebraic steps, and include units or domain restrictions where relevant.

chapters.title: Permutations and Combinations

content.overview: Permutations count ordered arrangements, while combinations count selections where order does not matter.
study_notes: Permutation: ■P■ = n!/(n−r)!.
Combination: ■C■ = n!/[r!(n−r)!].
For arrangements with repeated identical objects, divide by the factorials of repeat counts.
content.short_questions:
How do permutations and combinations differ?

   Answer: Permutation considers order; combination does not.

Bangladesh HSC Higher Mathematics | First & Second Paper                                                                                      Page 5

What is the value of 0!?

   Answer: 1.
content.long_questions:
How many ways can 3 students be selected from 8 students?

   Solution: Order does not matter, so use combinations: ■C■ = 8!/(3!5!) = (8×7×6)/(3×2×1) = 56 ways.

mcqs.content: ■P■ equals: A. 10 B. 20 C. 25 D. 60 Answer: B
■C■ equals: A. 10 B. 20 C. 25 D. 60 Answer: A

content.answer_tip: Exam tip: State the formula or theorem, show the substitution and algebraic steps, and include units or domain restrictions where relevant.

chapters.source_text:
1ST PAPER — Chapter 5: Permutations and Combinations
Chapter overview
Permutations count ordered arrangements, while combinations count selections where order does not matter.

Key concepts and important formulas
• n! = n(n−1)…1 and 0! = 1.

• Permutation: ■P■ = n!/(n−r)!.

• Combination: ■C■ = n!/[r!(n−r)!].

• ■C■ = ■C■■■.

• For arrangements with repeated identical objects, divide by the factorials of repeat counts.

Short-answer practice — answers
How do permutations and combinations differ?

   Answer: Permutation considers order; combination does not.

What is the value of 0!?

   Answer: 1.

Long-answer practice — worked solution
How many ways can 3 students be selected from 8 students?

   Solution: Order does not matter, so use combinations: ■C■ = 8!/(3!5!) = (8×7×6)/(3×2×1) = 56 ways.

Multiple-choice questions
1. ■P■ equals:

A. 10    B. 20    C. 25      D. 60

Answer: B

2. ■C■ equals:

A. 10    B. 20    C. 25      D. 60

Answer: A

Exam tip: State the formula or theorem, show the substitution and algebraic steps, and include units or domain restrictions where relevant.

chapters.title: Trigonometric Ratios

content.overview: Trigonometry relates angles to ratios of sides in right triangles and is extended to the unit circle.
study_notes: sinθ = opposite/hypotenuse; cosθ = adjacent/hypotenuse; tanθ = opposite/adjacent.
tanθ = sinθ/cosθ.
sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
1+tan²θ = sec²θ and 1+cot²θ = cosec²θ.
Use the correct quadrant to determine the sign of each ratio.
content.short_questions:
What is tanθ in terms of sine and cosine?

   Answer: tanθ = sinθ/cosθ, where cosθ ≠ 0.
State the fundamental Pythagorean identity.

   Answer: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
content.long_questions:
If sinθ = 3/5 and θ is acute, find cosθ and tanθ.

   Solution: cosθ = √(1−9/25) = 4/5 because θ is acute. Hence tanθ = (3/5)/(4/5) = 3/4.

mcqs.content: If sinθ = 0.6 and θ is acute, cosθ is: A. 0.4 B. 0.6 C. 0.8 D. 1.6 Answer: C
tanθ equals: A. cosθ/sinθ B. sinθ/cosθ C. 1/sinθ D. 1/cosθ Answer: B

content.answer_tip: Exam tip: State the formula or theorem, show the substitution and algebraic steps, and include units or domain restrictions where relevant. Bangladesh HSC Higher Mathematics | First & Second Paper Page 6

1ST PAPER — Chapter 6: Trigonometric Ratios
Chapter overview
Trigonometry relates angles to ratios of sides in right triangles and is extended to the unit circle.

Key concepts and important formulas
• sinθ = opposite/hypotenuse; cosθ = adjacent/hypotenuse; tanθ = opposite/adjacent.

• tanθ = sinθ/cosθ.

• sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

• 1+tan²θ = sec²θ and 1+cot²θ = cosec²θ.

• Use the correct quadrant to determine the sign of each ratio.

Short-answer practice — answers
What is tanθ in terms of sine and cosine?

   Answer: tanθ = sinθ/cosθ, where cosθ ≠ 0.
State the fundamental Pythagorean identity.

   Answer: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

Long-answer practice — worked solution
If sinθ = 3/5 and θ is acute, find cosθ and tanθ.

   Solution: cosθ = √(1−9/25) = 4/5 because θ is acute. Hence tanθ = (3/5)/(4/5) = 3/4.

Multiple-choice questions
1. If sinθ = 0.6 and θ is acute, cosθ is:

A. 0.4   B. 0.6     C. 0.8    D. 1.6

Answer: C

2. tanθ equals:

A. cosθ/sinθ      B. sinθ/cosθ       C. 1/sinθ   D. 1/cosθ

Answer: B

chapters.title: Trigonometric Ratios of Associated

content.overview: Associated-angle identities express trigonometric functions of angles related by complements, supplements and half/full turns.
study_notes: sin(90°−θ)=cosθ; cos(90°−θ)=sinθ.
sin(180°−θ)=sinθ; cos(180°−θ)=−cosθ.
sin(180°+θ)=−sinθ; cos(180°+θ)=−cosθ.
sin(360°−θ)=−sinθ; cos(360°−θ)=cosθ.
The sign of a ratio depends on the quadrant.
content.short_questions:
What is sin(90°−θ)?

   Answer: cosθ.
In which quadrants is cosine negative?

   Answer: The second and third quadrants.
content.long_questions:
Evaluate sin150° + cos120°.

   Solution: sin150° = sin30° = 1/2. cos120° = −cos60° = −1/2. Sum = 0.

sin(360°−θ) equals: A. sinθ B. −sinθ C. cosθ D. −cosθ Answer: B

chapters.title: Functions and Graphs of Functions

content.overview:
A function assigns exactly one output to each input in its domain. Functions can be represented algebraically, graphically or by
tables.
study_notes: Domain is the set of permitted inputs; range is the set of resulting outputs.
A vertical-line test determines whether a graph represents y as a function of x.
For f(x)=mx+c, the graph is a straight line.
Composite function: (f■g)(x)=f(g(x)).
An inverse function exists when the function is one-to-one on its domain.
content.short_questions:
What is the domain of a function?

   Answer: The set of all allowed input values.

Bangladesh HSC Higher Mathematics | First & Second Paper                                                                                      Page 7

What does the vertical-line test check?

   Answer: Whether any vertical line intersects the graph more than once.
content.long_questions:
If f(x)=2x+3, find f■¹(x).

   Solution: Let y=2x+3. Interchange x and y: x=2y+3. Then y=(x−3)/2. Thus f■¹(x)=(x−3)/2.

mcqs.content: If f(x)=x² on all real numbers, it is: A. One-to-one B. Not one-to-one C. Constant D. Undefined Answer: B
The domain of f(x)=1/x excludes: A. 1 B. −1 C. 0 D. 2 Answer: C

chapters.title: Differentiation

content.overview:
Differentiation measures instantaneous rate of change and gives the gradient of a curve. It is central to tangent, velocity and
optimisation problems.
study_notes: Derivative definition: f′(x)=lim■→■[f(x+h)−f(x)]/h.
Power rule: d(x■)/dx = nx■■¹.
d(sin x)/dx=cos x; d(cos x)/dx=−sin x.
Product rule: (uv)′=u′v+uv′; quotient rule: (u/v)′=(u′v−uv′)/v².
Chain rule: d[f(g(x))]/dx=f′(g(x))g′(x).
content.short_questions:
What does the derivative represent geometrically?

   Answer: The gradient of the tangent to the curve at a point.
Differentiate x■.

   Answer: The derivative is 5x■.
content.long_questions:
Differentiate y = (3x²+1)(x−2).

   Solution: Using the product rule: dy/dx = 6x(x−2)+(3x²+1)(1) = 9x²−12x+1.

mcqs.content: d(x■)/dx equals: A. x³ B. 4x³ C. 4x■ D. x■ Answer: B
The derivative of cos x is: A. sin x B. −sin x C. cos x D. −cos x Answer: B

content.answer_tip: Exam tip: State the formula or theorem, show the substitution and algebraic steps, and include units or domain restrictions where relevant. Bangladesh HSC Higher Mathematics | First & Second Paper Page 8

chapters.title: Integration

content.overview: Integration is the reverse process of differentiation and is used to find antiderivatives and accumulated quantities such as area.
study_notes: ∫x■dx = x■■¹/(n+1)+C for n≠−1.
∫1/x dx = ln|x|+C.
∫cos x dx = sin x+C; ∫sin x dx = −cos x+C.
Definite integral: ∫■■f(x)dx = F(b)−F(a).
Area between a curve and x-axis requires attention to sign and intervals.
content.short_questions:
Why is an arbitrary constant added to an indefinite integral?

   Answer: Because all antiderivatives of a function differ by an additive constant.
Evaluate ∫2x dx.

   Answer: x²+C.
content.long_questions:
Evaluate ∫■²(3x²+1)dx.

   Solution: An antiderivative is x³+x. Evaluate: (8+2)−(0+0)=10.

mcqs.content: ∫x²dx equals: A. 2x+C B. x³/3+C C. x²/2+C D. 3x+C Answer: B
The derivative of an antiderivative F(x) is: A. 0 B. f(x) C. F(x)² D. C Answer: B

chapters.title: Real Numbers and Inequalities

content.overview:
Real numbers include rational and irrational numbers. Inequalities compare quantities and are solved using order properties of the
real number system.

chapters.title: Conics

content.overview:
Conic sections are curves formed by intersecting a plane with a double cone. The main conics are the circle, parabola, ellipse and
hyperbola.
study_notes: A parabola is the locus of points equidistant from a focus and directrix.
For y²=4ax, focus=(a,0), directrix x=−a.
For x²/a²+y²/b²=1, the ellipse has semi-axes a and b.
For x²/a²−y²/b²=1, the hyperbola opens along the x-axis.
Eccentricity distinguishes conics: ellipse e<1, parabola e=1, hyperbola e>1.
content.short_questions:
Define a parabola.

   Answer: The locus of a point whose distance from a fixed focus equals its perpendicular distance from a fixed directrix.
What is the eccentricity of a parabola?

   Answer: 1.
content.long_questions:
Find the focus and directrix of y²=12x.

   Solution: Compare y²=4ax: 4a=12, so a=3. Focus=(3,0); directrix is x=−3.

mcqs.content: The eccentricity of an ellipse is: A. Equal to 1 B. Less than 1 C. Greater than 1 D. Always 2 Answer: B
For y²=4ax, the focus is: A. (0,a) B. (a,0) C. (−a,0) D. (0,−a) Answer: B

content.overview: Statics studies forces on bodies in equilibrium. A body is in equilibrium when the resultant force and resultant moment are zero.

content.overview:
This chapter applies vectors and kinematics to particle motion in two dimensions, including projectile motion and motion under
gravity.
study_notes: Velocity is the time rate of change of position; acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
For constant acceleration, v=u+at and s=ut+½at² in one dimension.
Projectile horizontal velocity is constant when air resistance is neglected.
For launch and landing at the same level: T=2u sinθ/g; H=u²sin²θ/(2g); R=u²sin2θ/g.
At the highest point of projectile motion, vertical velocity is zero.
content.short_questions:

   Answer: Two-dimensional motion of an object projected into the air and then moving under gravity, neglecting air resistance.
What is the vertical velocity at the highest point?

   Answer: Zero.
content.long_questions:

   Solution: T=2u sinθ/g = 2×20×0.5/10 = 2 s.

chapters.title: Measures of Dispersion and Probability

content.overview:
Statistics summarises data, while measures of dispersion describe its spread. Probability quantifies uncertainty for random
events.
study_notes: Range = maximum − minimum.
Variance is the mean squared deviation from the arithmetic mean (with convention depending on population/sample).
Standard deviation is the positive square root of variance.
For equally likely outcomes, P(A)=favourable outcomes/total outcomes.
P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B); for independent events P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B).
content.short_questions:
What is range?

   Answer: The difference between the largest and smallest observations.
What is the probability of an impossible event?

   Answer: Zero.
content.long_questions:
A fair die is rolled once. Find the probability of obtaining an even number.

   Solution: Even outcomes are {2,4,6}, three of six equally likely outcomes. Probability=3/6=1/2.

mcqs.content: The range of 2, 4, 9, 10 is: A. 6 B. 7 C. 8 D. 12 Answer: C
For independent events A and B: A. P(A∩B)=P(A)+P(B) B. P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) C. P(A)=P(B) D. P(A∪B)=0 Answer: B
